location_constraints.name: Authoritative records and private transaction state remain separate
conditions: Current typed records/payloads and temporary maintenance/coordination state occupy disjoint selected runtime paths.
Disjoint scopes do not imply distinct hosts, devices or protection against arbitrary external writers.
location_constraints.rationale: Maintenance exclusion and staged recovery are physical safeguards, not engineering activity history.

proposed.choice: Use a separately versioned current-handoff contract for requirement/design bases, checked milestone progress, current assessments and selective retained support.
proposed.rationale: The subordinate MOD-011 contract defines v4 current accounts, safe replacement and compact historical completion; MOD-010 defines v2 scoped operations. Typed identities and explicit applicability preserve decision meaning without a mandatory attempt archive or reinterpretation of v3. Current source implements the normalized schema and task dispatch; passing execution and project adoption require their own evidence. Historical import is explicit and does not promote old judgments.
alternatives: Silently reinterpret v3 Proposal or milestone judgments.
Indefinite dual-write or fallback runtime between obsolete internals.
consequences: Implement v4 current accounts directly over SQLite; no intermediate filesystem backend, dual writes or legacy runtime fallback. Store queryable relationships in tables and selected bulky payloads as managed named files.
Preserve required migration originals and provenance; explicit import cannot promote old judgments to new approval.
SR-074–078 govern selected backup, restore, transfer, migration and discovery. Qualify these prerequisites before runtime adoption; authoring the current design requires no database.

Database schema 1 uses typed current-account tables and constrained relationships; maintenance supplies selected-scope integrity manifests and staged replacement with retained prior bytes. Revisions include store incarnation to reject pre-restore tokens.
revisit_when: External compatibility disposition or the separate store migration changes the supported adoption boundary.
